labelQuoting: UI labels inside steps are wrapped in curly quotes (“…”). scripts/website/check_help.mjs verifies each one exists verbatim in StickDeathInfinity/**/*.swift or android/**/*.kt.

statuses.source-implemented: Behavior read from the current repository source. Not a device or App Store verification receipt.
statuses.verified-on-device: Reserved for topics with recorded device evidence. No topic currently carries this status.
statuses.unavailable: The control exists or is described, but the connected service is not configured or the action reports unavailability.

articles.title: Start a project and choose its canvas
keywords: new animation project presets dimensions fps setup width height portrait landscape square custom
steps: iOS: in the project library choose “+ New Animation”, type a name into “Project name…”, pick a canvas preset (Portrait, Landscape, Square, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, SD or HD) or enter a custom width and height, choose a frame rate, then choose “Create Project →”.
Canvas sides accept “16–4096 pixels per side” and the frame rate accepts “Whole numbers from 1 to 60 FPS”. “Swap width and height” exchanges the two numbers.

iOS: inside Studio, open “Project Settings” to change the name, dimensions, FPS or background, then choose “Apply Changes →”. Canvas changes keep artwork at its original position and only change the visible area; nothing is scaled. Undo restores the previous settings and “Reload current settings” discards unapplied edits.
Android: the creation form and the editor’s “Project settings” share the same eight named presets, custom width/height from 16 to 4096 pixels and exact integer FPS from 1 to 60.
limits: Resizing may be unavailable for historical flattened images, pixel effects or a smaller size that would discard fill coverage.
A project is stored on the device. This website cannot create or open projects.
Android behavior is read from source; compilation and device checks are deferred.

articles.title: Find, duplicate, back up and restore projects
keywords: library search sort duplicate recently deleted restore backup sdiproject import storage cache refresh
steps: Use “Search projects” and “Sort projects” in the library to find a saved project. Open a project’s menu for “Duplicate Project”, “Move to Recently Deleted” and “Save Project Backup to Files”.
Open “Recently Deleted” and choose “Restore” to bring a project back. Projects remain on the device until restored; there is no automatic deletion.

To move an editable project between devices, choose “Save Project Backup to Files”, complete the Files save, then on the other device choose “Import project backup” and select the .sdiproject file. Validation finishes before a separate project with a new identity is created; the original is never overwritten.

Open “Storage”, then “Refresh usage” to measure Documents and disk caches. “Clear working cache” releases cached frame encodings from memory only; it does not delete projects, history, media, backups or exports and does not free disk space.
limits: MP4, GIF and PNG exports are not editable backups. Keep the .sdiproject file if you need the editable project later.
An unsupported, damaged or oversized backup reports an error and imports nothing; the original file is kept.
Recently Deleted is recoverable storage, not a permanent-delete feature.

articles.title: Save and return to the project library
keywords: back projects persist reopen autosave unsaved storage failed save indicator
steps: Finish the current edit and use “Save project” when it is offered; watch the Studio save indicator for the device-save result.
Use the Studio back control or “Projects” to return to the library. If saving reports an error, keep the editor open and read the message.
Select the project in the library to continue editing. On Android, Back waits for a successful save and a write failure keeps the open document and its history.
limits: A save error is not success. Local data can be lost when the app is uninstalled unless you kept a backup.
Android projects use the Android-local envelope; see the Android topic for what can and cannot be exchanged with iOS.

articles.title: Draw on an editable layer
keywords: pencil pen brush marker crayon eraser bucket fill eyedropper shapes text color size stroke tool toolbar undo redo
steps: Open a project and select a visible, unlocked layer in “Layers”.

iOS: choose a tool in the single white floating toolbar, which snaps vertically to either canvas edge. Tools: “Move”, “Lasso”, “Wand”, “Brush”, “Pencil”, “Pen”, “Marker”, “Crayon”, “Line”, “Rect”, “Circle”, “Fill”, “Dropper”, “Eraser”, “Smudge”, “Sharpen”, “Dodge”, “Burn”, “Blur”, “Text”, “Hand” and “Zoom”. Tool settings, including Hand, Zoom and Fit, open in the one dismissible options popup.
Draw on the canvas. “UNDO” reverses the last committed edit and “REDO” restores it.

Android: choose “Pencil” with one of eight brush families (Round, Stipple, Grain, Rough Pen, Calligraphy, Dip Pen, Halftone, Hatch), “Eraser”, the shapes “Line”, “Rectangle”, “Ellipse”, “Triangle”, “Diamond”, “Star” and “Arrow”, “Text”, “Fill”, “Eyedropper”, “Lasso”, “Move” or “Hand”. Each brush family remembers its own width, opacity, smoothing and nib angle.
limits: The Android eraser clears marks inside the active layer only and reveals lower layers and the white canvas; it does not remove imported-photo backgrounds.
Hidden or locked layers reject drawing on both platforms.
Android behavior is read from source; device verification is deferred.

articles.title: Layers: order, visibility, opacity, blend and lock
keywords: invisible missing hidden lock opacity stack order show hide blend mode multiply screen overlay glow thumbnail rename duplicate
steps: Open “Layers”. Each row shows a thumbnail, its name and an eye control that toggles visibility. Use the up and down arrows to reorder, “Duplicate” to copy a layer, “Rename layer” to change its name and “Delete selected layer” to remove it.
Adjust “Opacity” for the selected layer. A hidden layer or zero opacity makes its content invisible without deleting it.

Choose a “BLEND MODE”. iOS offers 18 modes: “Normal”, “Darken”, “Multiply”, “Color Burn”, “Linear Burn”, “Lighten”, “Screen”, “Color Dodge”, “Linear Dodge (Add)”, “Overlay”, “Soft Light”, “Hard Light”, “Difference”, “Exclusion”, “Hue”, “Saturation”, “Color” and “Luminosity”.

Set a “LOCK MODE”: “Free” allows every edit, “Pos” locks position, “Alpha” preserves existing transparency and “Full” blocks edits. Set the lock to “Free” before transforming artwork. “Glow” adds an optional layer glow with radius and strength.

Android layers are shared across every frame and support add, select, reorder, visibility, opacity, lock and 16 blend modes (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity).
limits: Do not delete a project to recover hidden content; check visibility, opacity, lock mode and stack order first.
The blend catalogue, order and formulas are ported from PhotoCraft under the MIT License; see Attribution.
Android has no Linear Burn or Linear Dodge mode.

articles.title: Lasso artwork, then move, resize or rotate it
keywords: selection dotted outline box marquee polygon freehand rectangle transform hand nudge align rotate keep proportions scale
steps: Choose “Lasso” in the Studio toolbar. In its options choose “Drawings”, “Image on active layer” or “Drawings + image”, then Freehand, Rectangle or Polygon. These targets select whole objects; enclose the whole active-layer image to select it.

Finish the outline. A nonempty selection switches to “Move” automatically, closes the options popup and shows a transform box. Drag inside the box to move, use its corner handles to resize or the red handle to rotate. “Hand” pans the canvas instead of moving artwork.

Drawing-only selection starts with free width/height resizing; enable “Keep proportions” in the Move options if needed. Image and mixed groups keep their proportions. Use “Nudge distance” and “Align” for exact placement, or the “SCALE & ROTATE” sliders with “Apply transform”. Images stay inside the canvas, including their rotated bounds.

If only the outline appears, check the target, active layer, visibility and lock mode, stop playback and read any save or selection error. Set the layer lock to “Free”. “UNDO” reverses a committed transform.
limits: Move transforms at most 1,024 drawing objects together with at most one selected active-layer image.
Hidden and transform-locked layers are excluded from selection.
Current source behavior, not proof that an installed build contains this update.

articles.title: Move just part of an imported image
keywords: lasso pixels fragment photo picture cut selection lift partial delete resize wand tolerance color region
steps: Select the imported image’s layer. It must be visible, unlocked, fully opaque, in Normal blend, with no drawings or glow.
In the Lasso options choose “Image pixels → Move” and enclose the part you want. This is a New selection; Add and Subtract are not available for pixel lifting.

Completing the outline lifts the selected pixels onto a new selected layer and switches to Move. The remainder stays on the original layer and the original source bytes are preserved. Drag the box or use its handles; “UNDO” restores the original arrangement.
For regions selected by color instead, choose “Wand”, tap visible image pixels, adjust “Tolerance” and “Sample colors”, then use its Move on canvas action.
limits: Source images are limited to four million pixels for pixel lifting and Wand selection.
Empty, unsupported or stale selections report an error instead of pretending a move succeeded.

articles.title: Add pictures, photos, library images and video frames
keywords: photo library files camera paste image library packs download background gradient solid magic cut background cut rotoscope video frame trace
steps: Open “Add Picture”. Choose “Photo Library” or “Files” for a still image, “Take Photo” to capture a still (preview, then add), or “Paste an image” for one copied JPEG, PNG or HEIF. Nothing is added until you choose “Add to current frame”; each import becomes its own image layer and never replaces an existing image.
“Rotoscope / Video” traces one frame from a self-contained MP4 or MOV up to 16 MB and 4 megapixels, extracted at the current Studio playhead and added on a separate layer.

“Image Library” has 207 bundled pictures and six optional packs with 1,818 more: 1-Bit Scenery (458), 1-Bit Characters and Props (615), 1-Bit Platformer (391), Monochrome RPG (135), Micro Roguelike (160) and Smoke and Explosions (59). Each pack has its own Download button and size; wait for “Pictures verified and available offline.” before relying on it. “Remove download” removes only the library copy, not pictures already in projects.
“Background Library” adds one of 16 generated presets (8 gradients and 8 solid colors) behind the drawings of the current frame. “Magic Cut” removes a background from an imported image.
limits: Camera captures above 16 megapixels or 16 MB are rejected; photos are not saved to Photos or uploaded.
Background Cut supports imported images up to 4 megapixels and 16 MB each.
Camera recording and whole-video timeline import are not available.
Library pictures are Kenney CC0 assets; see Attribution. Pack downloads need a connection and sufficient space.

articles.title: Add, duplicate, reorder or remove frames
keywords: timeline copy pose delete last frame undo range reverse paste cut
steps: Select the frame next to where you want to work. The plus button adds a blank frame; “Duplicate frame” starts from the selected pose.

Use “Copy frame”, “Cut frame” and “Paste frame after this” to move poses. “Frame range / timing…” works on several frames: “Duplicate selected range”, “Reverse selected range”, “Move earlier”, “Move later” or delete the range.
“DEL” removes the selected frame, not the project. At least one frame must remain, audio clips keep their times, and one “UNDO” restores a removed range.
Android: add, duplicate and delete frames, with “Copy frame”, “Cut frame” and “Paste frame” in the timeline. Duplicates receive fresh frame and stroke identities.
limits: Projects are limited to 1,000 frames.
A layer lock can prevent destructive operations on its content.

articles.title: Change exposure, retime a range or insert tweens
keywords: hold duration fps playback timeline speed frames ticks tween in-between easing
steps: Select a frame and open “Frame exposure” to choose its hold in ticks. A frame held for 3 ticks at 12 FPS lasts 3/12 of a second; each tick lasts exactly 1/FPS seconds.
“Frame range / timing…” then “Apply frame timing” scales every hold in the range independently, rounded to whole ticks; a result outside 1–600 ticks disables the action.

“Tween to next frame…” then “Insert in-betweens” bakes 1–24 editable in-between frames between two adjacent frames with matching drawings and image layers. Duplicate a frame, move its artwork for the next pose, then tween.
Android changes exposure ticks per frame and previews playback at project FPS; tweening is not implemented there.
limits: Tween is limited to 65,536 generated points and 1,024 generated drawings and images per operation.
Changing project FPS changes tick speed. Saved audio timing stays absolute; retiming frames does not stretch audio.

articles.title: Use onion skin and the grid
keywords: previous next frame overlay guides onion grid alignment ghosts spacing
steps: iOS: open “Project Settings” and find the “TOOLS” rows. Turn on “Onion” and choose “Edit” to set previous and next ghost counts and opacity; farther frames fade.
Turn on “Grid” and choose “Edit” for spacing and opacity. The grid moves and zooms with the canvas.
Android: toggle “Onion skin” in the editor; previous frames show in red and next frames in blue. Grid guides save with the project and follow canvas zoom.
limits: Guides are editor overlays, never layers. Ghosts and grid are hidden during playback and never included in exports on either platform.

articles.title: Add a sound and place it on the timeline
keywords: sound library audio music effects search favorites preview track volume mute waveform snap trim split voice
steps: Open “AUDIO”, then “+ Add Sound”. Search the 2,127-effect CC0 library or choose a category. Preview a result before adding it; the preview button does not insert a clip.
Choose a destination with “Add sounds to track” and use the plus button beside the sound. The clip is added at the captured audio playhead. Read any import or save error before treating it as added.
Select the clip in the timeline. Drag it to move and drag its edges to trim. “Snap: ON” aligns to frames, the playhead and other clip edges; “Snap: OFF” allows free timing.
Adjust “Selected clip volume”, “Mute selected clip” and the track volume, then play the timeline. “Voice Maker” offers on-device synthesized speech clips.
limits: A muted clip or track, or zero volume, makes that preview silent.
PNG, Spritesheet and GIF exports contain no audio; MP4 includes the saved soundtrack.
Library waveforms are measured from real files; every entry keeps its creator and source URL.

articles.title: Import audio or a movie soundtrack from Files
keywords: audio mp4 mov video soundtrack interval speed pitch import files cancel local music
steps: In “AUDIO”, choose the destination “Track”, then “Import from Files”. For a movie, enable “Extract audio from a video” and choose an MP4 or MOV.
Set the source start and end and the “Video audio speed” before importing. Speed changes duration and pitch. The clip is added at the captured timeline playhead.
Wait for preparation and the real save result. Cancel stops preparation; changing the project can invalidate the captured destination. A failed import is not a silent successful clip.
Trim and position the imported clip. The original stays in Files.
limits: “Up to 16 MB / 5 min · mono or stereo · decoded sample limits apply”.
This flow does not record microphone input or upload your movie. Only use soundtracks you have rights to use.

articles.title: Fade curves, track pan and solo
keywords: fade in out curve linear equal power s-curve exponential logarithmic pan left right center solo silent mixer
steps: Select a clip and choose “Fade in / out”. Enter “Fade in (sec)” and “Fade out (sec)”, then pick a shape for “Fade in curve” and “Fade out curve”: “Linear”, “Equal Power”, “S-Curve”, “Exponential” or “Logarithmic”. A small glyph previews each curve. The inspector shows “No fades” until an envelope is applied.

Below the selected clip, the track row has a “Pan” slider from full left to full right. The value reads C at center, or L and R with a percentage; values within 4% of center snap to exact center. Pan applies to the whole track in preview and MP4 export.

Press the track’s “S” button to solo it. While any track is soloed, other tracks are silent and their clips show a notice. Press “S” again to unsolo; mute remains a separate per-track and per-clip control.
Play the timeline to hear fades, pan and solo together. Each change is one Undo step and saves with the project.
limits: Pan and solo are per track (1–4), not per clip. Clips still preparing (no asset) disable the track’s pan and solo controls.
Fade shapes, pan law and the mute/solo rule are ported from SoundCraft under the MIT License; see Attribution.
Android audio supports linear fades and per-track gain/mute only.

articles.title: Choose an export that fits your result
keywords: png sequence spritesheet atlas mp4 movie gif sound transparent white share files aac
steps: Open “Export” and choose “PNG”, “Spritesheet”, “MP4” or “GIF”.
“PNG” and “Spritesheet” render lossless frames with “Export frames” and an “Export background” of “White” or “Transparent”, plus a timing manifest. Spritesheet packs every frame into one atlas.

“MP4” renders H.264 video with saved project audio as stereo AAC; its background is “White” only (“Transparent (unsupported)”). “GIF” uses reduced colors, a white background and no audio, with a “GIF longest edge” of 320, 640 or 960 px or the original size.
Complete the export, then use “Share files / Save to Files”, “Share MP4 / Save to Files” or “Share GIF / Save to Files”. “Cancel export” stops rendering.
limits: No watermark is added to exports. PNG and GIF exports do not include sound.
GIF supports up to 240 frames at 1–50 fps within 8.4 million total frame pixels.
An exported picture or movie is not an editable project backup; use Save Project Backup to Files for that.

articles.title: Ask Spatter for guidance or a local motion recipe
keywords: assistant chat guide help recipe walk run jump wave stick figure preferences memory
steps: Open the Spatter panel in Studio and describe what you want to do. Answers cite the current guide revision and describe controls; they never change your project by themselves.

For motion, open “Stick figure examples” and choose walking, running, jumping or waving. Procedural recipes append 8–20 editable stick-figure frames at the project FPS; choose “Apply local edit” to commit or “Cancel local edit” to discard.

“Local memory preferences…” is off by default. Turn on “Use my local preferences”, choose guidance level and animation focus, then “Save preferences”. “Reset saved preferences” deletes this account’s local record.
limits: Spatter does not learn from conversation history, inspect your account, or claim a support ticket was sent.
Preferences stay on the device, separately scoped to each account and guest.
Guidance describes current source and may differ from an older installed app.

articles.title: Submit a video for review and manage permissions
keywords: publish upload youtube channel feed marketing review approval permission revoke consent terms
steps: After an MP4 export choose “Submit this MP4 for review”, or in Profile choose “Choose MP4 and keep upload copy”. Sign in first.

Choose destinations separately: “StickDeath Infinity home feed”, “Official SDI YouTube channel” and “SDI social marketing reuse”. Only selected destinations may be reviewed. Confirm the rights toggle and read the terms with “Read publishing terms”, choose “Made for kids” or “Not made for kids”, then “Submit for review”.

A receipt is not publication. Every Spatter-generated video also needs the owner’s approval of the exact render in the admin command center before any feed, channel or social release; a revision invalidates approval.
Use “Pause”, “Resume upload”, “Remove upload copy” or “Cancel upload and remove copy” to manage the staged copy. Your original export and editable project are never deleted by these actions.
limits: “Uploading is unavailable until the private service and current publishing terms are configured.” Nothing auto-publishes.
Channel and social versions may include SDI branding; the editable original is retained.
Registered reviews keep a separate permission-withdrawal workflow.

articles.title: Account, plan and deletion status
keywords: login profile username billing subscription plan price support ticket delete account website
steps: This website has no sign-in, checkout or billing. The account page states whether a portal is connected; today it is not.
In the app, Profile shows “Plan unavailable” for signed-in accounts and “On-device guest” when you are not signed in. No plan, price or renewal date is displayed because none is configured.

Profile offers “Delete account” and Settings shows “Account deletion unavailable”: the deletion service currently reports that it is unavailable, nothing is deleted and your projects stay on the device.
limits: Approved pricing and public distribution links need a separate release update; none are shown here.
Authenticated support intake is not connected. Use the local problem-summary tool on this page and do not include passwords, payment data or private project contents.

articles.title: Check rights before sharing imported artwork
keywords: license attribution copyright asset image audio commercial cc0 credits kenney font
steps: Use artwork and audio you own or have permission to use. Bundled library pictures and sounds are CC0; their creator and source URL travel with each imported asset.
Android exports a “Project asset credits JSON” listing bundled assets with recorded provenance. Keep the accompanying license information for any asset you import yourself.
Check the terms for your intended use before publishing the final animation. See the Attribution page for fonts, ported formulas and asset packs.
limits: A plan name or paid subscription does not grant blanket commercial rights to every imported asset.
This website does not issue licenses or accept private project uploads.

articles.title: Android scope, exports and project interchange
keywords: zip sequence manifest png mp4 gif spritesheet backup restore import sdi interchange document picker limit
steps: Stop playback and choose “Export”. Options: “Current frame PNG”, “PNG sequence ZIP” with a timing manifest, “Spritesheet PNG + timing ZIP”, “MP4 video + project audio” (H.264 plus AAC), “Animated GIF (looping)”, “Editable Android project backup” and “Project asset credits JSON”. Choose a destination in Android’s document picker.
“Import image” adds a still PNG or JPEG from Files as project-owned artwork; “Import audio from Files” adds WAV or device-supported compressed audio to one of four tracks.

“Restore project backup (.sdi / Android)” reopens an Android backup or imports a subset of iOS .sdiproject backups: round pen/pencil/brush strokes, frames with exposure and Normal layers with order, visibility, opacity and locks. Imports with images, audio, text, fills, effects, guides, non-Normal blends or other brush families are rejected whole, before anything is saved.
limits: Exports use a 4-megapixel canvas limit and 256 MiB staging. MP4 and GIF are limited to 120 seconds; MP4 needs even dimensions; spritesheets stay within 8 megapixels and an 8192-pixel edge.
Transparent export is not implemented on Android. The Android backup (.sdiandroid.json) is not the iOS format and Android-to-iOS editable export is not implemented.
All Android behavior is read from source. Compilation, emulator and device acceptance are deferred, not passed.
